samples.summary: revocableDocStore revokes the handle, not the capabilities already taken from it: a data property or bound method read while the session was an editor keeps full write access after the downgrade
samples.evidence: In the live branch, `get` returns `raw` verbatim for non-functions (read-only.ts:199) and a function bound to the REAL store for methods (read-only.ts:202), and both are passed on unchanged by `pageSetupGuardedStore` (view/editor.ts:3312-3318). `readOnlyDocStore` deliberately hides data properties for exactly this reason — its own comment (read-only.ts:89-96) calls `YorkieDocStore.doc` "the CRDT handle, whose `update()` is the documented write path". So while the editor is alive, `editor.getStore().doc` yields that handle and `const f = editor.getStore().insertText` yields a writer bound to the real store. Neither is routed through the proxy again, so flipping `disposed` (view/editor.ts:4475) revokes neither: after an editor→viewer downgrade a stale holder calls `f('b1', 0, 'x')` or `capturedYorkieDoc.update(...)` and the write lands in the shared CRDT. This contradicts the claim in EditorAPI.isDisposed's doc ("the handles ... have gone read-only, copies already taken included"). I found no current in-repo holder that captures a method or field rather than the object (docs-find-bar captures the Doc; docs-formatting-toolbar re-fetches getStore() per call), so I could not complete the chain to a shipped exploit — hence medium confidence — but the gate reads as complete while it is not.

samples.summary: The entire downgrade/revocation boundary added here is client-side; with the default YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE=false the Yorkie server still accepts writes from a viewer-role or revoked share token
samples.evidence: The comment at shared-document.tsx:1095 states it plainly: under the default `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE=false` the docs read-only wrapper "is the write boundary the visitor actually meets". packages/documentation/developers/self-hosting.md:185 confirms the default is shadow mode — "log the decision, allow everything" — and packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-auth.controller.ts:101 gates enforcement on that env var being the string 'true'. Attack: hold an editor share token, keep the Yorkie attach (the auth token is injected at attach, shared-document.tsx:1009), let the owner downgrade the link to viewer or delete it; the new 60s poll only reconfigures this tab's React tree, so a modified client, a devtools console call, or a client that simply never re-polls keeps pushing changes and the server accepts them. Pre-existing posture rather than introduced here, and the repo tracks flipping the flag as a release precondition — but this PR builds its stated revocation guarantee on top of it, so the guarantee is advisory against a non-cooperating client.

samples.summary: neuterMutations replaces EditorAPI members in place, so a captured bare method reference survives dispose() and still writes to the raw store
samples.evidence: `neuterMutations` assigns over `api[name]` (the `(api as unknown as Record<string, () => void>)[name] = noop` loop). The stated rationale is that async continuations resume on the same object reference — true for `editor.insertImage(...)`, but a holder that took the function itself (`const f = editor.setPageSetup`) keeps the original closure, which reaches `writePageSetup` and writes straight to the raw `docStore` at editor.ts:2301 — that call is NOT routed through `revocableStore`, unlike the getStore() variant the diff fixed at editor.ts:3307. I grepped packages/frontend/src for bare method captures and found none, so this is currently unreachable; reporting it because the in-place strategy is documented as the reason the revocation is complete.

samples.summary: The slides mount effect now re-runs on a readOnlyMount downgrade, and its CRDT seeding/migration writes are not gated on read-only (docs-view and notes-view gate theirs)
samples.evidence: Adding `readOnlyMount` to the deps (slides-view.tsx:1235) means an editor→viewer downgrade re-executes the whole effect body as a viewer. That body writes to the CRDT before any role check: `doc.update(...)` for a staged PPTX import (slides-view.tsx:252) and `ensureSlidesRoot(doc, ...)` (slides-view.tsx:282), whose second `doc.update()` block runs unconditionally (yorkie-slides-store.ts:246). The equivalent seeds are role-gated in the sibling views — `if (!readOnly && !ensureTree(doc)) return;` (docs-view.tsx:354) and `if (!readOnly) ensureText(doc);` (notes-view.tsx:133) — and slides-view.tsx:276-281 already flags the ungated migration as a known gap. In practice the remount is likely a no-op because the first (editor) mount backfilled the fields and cleared the pending import, so I could not show a write actually reaching the server on the downgrade path.

samples.summary: A revoked or downgraded share link keeps its old authority for up to SHARE_LINK_REVALIDATE_MS of active use, and indefinitely while the tab is backgrounded
samples.evidence: `refetchInterval: SHARE_LINK_REVALIDATE_MS` (shared-document.tsx:1115) with react-query's default `refetchIntervalInBackground: false` means the poll pauses whenever the tab is not focused; `refetchOnWindowFocus: true` only closes that on the next focus. The window in which a downgraded editor keeps writing is therefore 60s of foreground use and unbounded in the background, and every write in that window lands in the shared CRDT because the server is in shadow mode by default. Reported as a hardening note on the size of the residual window, not as a defect in the mechanism.

samples.summary: The disposal gate reuses MUTATING_METHODS, a denylist whose own sibling file argues denylists fail open
samples.evidence: read-only.ts:6-19 explains at length that a list of mutators to deny "fails *open*: the new write forwards, and the gate still reads as complete", and that this is exactly how #989 happened. The diff hoists `MUTATING_METHODS` to module scope and makes it the disposal gate as well as the read-only gate (`neuterMutations` is called from both `dispose()` and the `if (readOnly)` tail), doubling the blast radius of a forgotten entry. I walked the current EditorAPI surface (editor.ts:53-438) against the list and found no missing document-mutating member today — `restoreLocalCursor`, `resetAfterDocumentReplace` and `validateCursorPosition` touch cursor/layout state only — so this is a maintenance hazard, not a live hole.
searchedFor: enumerated EditorAPI members by grep on packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:53-438
grep 'docStore\\.' in packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts to find raw-store writes reachable from unlisted api members

verdict.reason: The described code is present exactly as claimed. In revocableDocStore's live path, non-function members are returned verbatim (read-only.ts:199) and methods are returned bound to the real target (read-only.ts:202), so a member copied off the handle while the editor was alive never passes back through the proxy and is unaffected when `disposed` flips (editor.ts:4475). pageSetupGuardedStore forwards both unchanged (editor.ts:3312-3318), so `editor.getStore().doc` yields YorkieDocStore's live CRDT handle — `private doc` is TypeScript-only (yorkie-doc-store.ts:577), and readOnlyDocStore hides data properties for precisely this reason (read-only.ts:89-96). This contradicts EditorAPI.isDisposed's documented contract that copies already taken have gone read-only (editor.ts:408-411), on the very downgrade path the dispose comment describes (editor.ts:4456-4474). No guard elsewhere closes it: getStore()/getDoc() deliberately carry no disposed check (editor.ts:3333-3339), and today's callers merely happen not to capture members (docs-find-bar captures the Doc, whose mutators re-enter the store proxy per call; formatting-toolbar/export re-fetch getStore()), which is coincidence rather than enforcement. In-lane for the security rubric because the repo states this client gate is the actual write boundary while the Yorkie auth webhook ships in shadow mode (editor.ts:4529-4533, read-only.ts:38-42). Major: a real revocation gap in an access-control boundary that reads as complete, even though I found no shipped exploit chain.

finding.evidence: The comment at shared-document.tsx:1095 states it plainly: under the default `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE=false` the docs read-only wrapper "is the write boundary the visitor actually meets". packages/documentation/developers/self-hosting.md:185 confirms the default is shadow mode — "log the decision, allow everything" — and packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-auth.controller.ts:101 gates enforcement on that env var being the string 'true'. verdict.reason: Every cited anchor is present as described. yorkie-auth.controller.ts:100-101 gates enforcement on the string 'true', and :111-119 converts any deny into an allow ("shadow") when the flag is unset, discarding the editor-role check at :217 and the revocation/expiry check via findByToken at :213. self-hosting.md:185 documents the default as false = "log the decision, allow everything", and :596 explicitly warns such a deployment "allows everything regardless". shared-document.tsx:1009 injects the share token at attach, and the new revalidation query at :1107-1119 only reconfigures this tab's React tree, with the comment at :1095 conceding the client-side read-only wrapper is the write boundary the visitor actually meets. I found no alternative server-side write gate for share-link CRDT traffic — writes go directly to Yorkie, whose only authorization hook is this webhook (docs/design/yorkie-auth-webhook.md:201-204; docs/design/sharing.md:208 confirms off by default). So a downgraded-to-viewer or revoked editor token still writes successfully in the stock configuration: an authorization gate exists in code but sits outside the enforced path by default. Documented release preconditions are an ops step, not a code guard rendering the vector unreachable, so already-guarded does not apply; missing/weakened access control is squarely in the Security lane, so out-of-scope does not either.

finding.summary: dispose()'s write revocation is bypassed by an in-flight EditorAPI.paste(): pasteContent() checks readOnly/pasting but not `disposed`, so a clipboard read that resumes after the editor was disposed for a role downgrade still writes to the shared CRDT
finding.evidence: Vector: an anonymous visitor on `/shared/:token` with an *editor* link opens the docs context menu and clicks Paste (`packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-context-menu.tsx:272` → `void editor.paste()`). `EditorAPI.paste` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:3974) awaits `navigator.clipboard.read()` / `readText()` — an await that can span a browser clipboard permission prompt, i.e. arbitrarily long. Meanwhile the share link is re-resolved every 60s (`SHARE_LINK_REVALIDATE_MS`, packages/frontend/src/app/shared/shared-document.tsx:88/1115); an `editor` → `viewer` downgrade flips `readOnly`, and the docs-view effect (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-view.tsx:565/590) calls `editor.dispose()` and rebuilds a read-only editor. The captured continuation then resumes and calls `textEditor.pasteContent({html,text})` (editor.ts:3997 / 4005) on the *old* TextEditor, which was constructed with `readOnly === false` (`const textEditor` at editor.ts:2503 is never nulled by dispose). `pasteContent` (text-editor.ts:1659-1667) gates only on `this.readOnly` and `this.pasting`; `this.disposed` — set by TextEditor.dispose at text-editor.ts:6069 — is NOT checked, so the paste falls through `pasteFromParts` → `runPaste` → `applyPastePlan` (text-editor.ts:1544) and writes through the still-writable YorkieDocStore into the shared document. Neutering `api.paste` in `neuterMutations` (editor.ts:1055-1073) cannot stop this: the no-op replaces the member, not the already-running closure. The repo's own precedent shows the required guard: `pastePlainTextFromClipboard` re-checks `this.disposed || this.pasting || this.readOnly` at text-editor.ts:4261 for exactly this reason, and `deferPaste` checks `!this.disposed` at text-editor.ts:1609. Impact is a write past a revoked permission: the docs comment at editor.ts:4497-4501 states the Yorkie auth webhook ships in shadow mode unless `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE=true`, so in a stock deployment this client-side gate *is* the write boundary for a downgrad

verdict.reason: The finding's core factual claim — that `TextEditor.pasteContent` gates only on `this.readOnly` and `this.pasting` and does NOT check `this.disposed` — is false in this repository. At packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:1671, `if (this.disposed) return;` is the FIRST guard in the method, evaluated before the readOnly check (:1673) and the pasting check (:1677). The preceding comment (:1660-1670) describes the reviewer's exact vector verbatim: that EditorAPI.paste() awaits navigator.clipboard.read() across a permission prompt, that EditorAPI.dispose() neutering api.paste only replaces the entry point for future calls while a suspended call "resumes in its own closure, on the TextEditor it captured," and that the motivating case is "the host rebuilding the editor because the share role dropped to viewer." dispose() arms the flag at :6080-6081 (`this.disposed = true;`). The `pastePlainTextFromClipboard` precedent the reviewer cites as the "required guard" already has its counterpart applied here — that sibling check lives at :4273 (`if (this.disposed || this.pasting || this.readOnly) return;`). The scenario is additionally pinned by a regression test at packages/docs/test/view/editor-read-only.test.ts:1093-1104 ("a paste that resumes after disposal writes nothing"), which suspends the clipboard read, disposes, releases, awaits, and asserts the document is unchanged; the control test at :1106-1116 shows the same paste does land on a live editor, so the assertion is not vacuous. The EditorAPI.paste call site at editor.ts:3995-4028 is as described and does reach pasteContent at :4018/:4026, but the resumed call returns at :1671 before any write, so pasteFromParts/runPaste/applyPastePlan is never entered and the downstream YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE reasoning is unreachable via this path. The line range the reviewer quoted (1659-1667) falls inside the guard's own explanatory comment.

finding.summary: After dispose(), getStore()/getDoc() still hand out fully writable handles for a non-read-only editor, so the new disposal-time revocation is name-list-only and bypassable by any stale holder that writes through those accessors
finding.evidence: `dispose()` (editor.ts:4434-4444) sets `disposed = true` and calls `neuterMutations(api)`, and its comment claims "Disposal is the only moment the host can revoke it". But `getStore: () => (readOnly ? readStore : pageSetupGuardedStore)` (editor.ts:3318) and `getDoc: () => doc` (editor.ts:3317-ish) are not touched by disposal, and for an editor built while the session could write, `readStore === docStore` (editor.ts:1123) and `doc = new Doc(readStore)` — i.e. both handles are live and writable after dispose. The pre-existing justification for leaving the accessors out of the allowlist (editor.ts:4503-4509: they are "both backed by `readOnlyDocStore` under `readOnly`, so their mutators are already dead") is true only for the read-only construction path; this delta reuses the same allowlist for a second condition where that premise does not hold. Concretely writable path: `DocsFindBar` builds `new FindReplaceState(editor.getDoc(), () => editor.getStore().snapshot())` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-find-bar.tsx:65-68) and `replaceActive`/`replaceAll` mutate through the captured `Doc` (packages/docs/src/view/find-replace.ts:79-86), which bypasses every neutered `api` member; `packages/frontend/src/app/harness/hunt/bridge.ts:250/330/386` also holds `editor.getDoc()`/`getStore()`. I could not prove a user-reachable interleaving for the find bar (React commits the dispose and the `editor`-keyed effect rebuild in the same flush), hence medium confidence — but any future async holder of `getDoc()`/`getStore()` writes straight past the revocation, and the accessors are the documented escape hatch, so the gate reads as covering more than it does.

verdict.reason: The claimed code is not present as described. The finding asserts that for a non-read-only editor `readStore === docStore` and `doc = new Doc(readStore)` are raw, writable handles untouched by disposal, making revocation "name-list-only". In the working tree, editor.ts:1138-1140 builds `revocableStore = readOnly ? docStore : revocableDocStore(docStore, () => disposed)`, `readStore = readOnly ? readOnlyDocStore(docStore) : revocableStore`, and `doc = new Doc(readStore)` — i.e. exactly the non-read-only case the finding says is unguarded is routed through a proxy keyed on the same `disposed` flag that `dispose()` sets (editor.ts:4475). read-only.ts:190-228 shows `revocableDocStore` switching every `get` to `readOnlyDocStore(store)` once revoked (line 197), where mutators become `noop` (lines 113-117), and refusing `set`/`defineProperty`/`deleteProperty`/`setPrototypeOf` (lines 209-216). `getStore()` (editor.ts:3339) returns `pageSetupGuardedStore`, a proxy over `revocableStore` that re-resolves members through it per call (editor.ts:3309-3319) and whose single intercepted method writes via `revocableStore.setPageSetup` (editor.ts:3304-3307). `getDoc()` (editor.ts:3338) returns a `Doc` whose ~30 mutators all delegate to `this.store` (document.ts:98-103, 289, 306, 674, 690). The concrete exploit path cited — docs-find-bar.tsx:66-67 capturing the handles and find-replace.ts:78-87 mutating through the captured `Doc` — therefore hits the revoked store and no-ops after dispose. The finding's own hedge (it could not demonstrate a reachable interleaving) is moot because the write path itself is dead.
